The '''Gigorans''' were a species of bipedal, sentient [[Primate/Legends|primates]] indigenous to the planet [[Gigor/Legends|Gigor]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]].

==Biology and Appearance==
Gigorans were large bipedal lumbering creatures covered in long white or pale-colored hair, which meant they were often mistaken for [[Wookiee/Legends|wookiees]], [[Wampa/Legends|wampa]]s or other ferocious creatures. They are well-muscled<ref name="AJ13">{{JournalCite|13|Alien Encounters (article series)}}</ref> had huge upper body strength<ref name="Gambler" /> with long sinuous limbs ending in heavy clawed paw-like feet and hands that had<ref name="AJ13" /> either three<ref name="AE">''[[Alien Encounters]]''</ref> or four digits with opposable thumbs.<ref name="AJ13" /> They had large lungs that took in a lot of air and when sleeping their respiration slowed immensely and they snored. Gigorans were powerful and were considered intimidating which made them a target for [[Slaver/Legends|slavers]].<ref name="Gambler" />

==History==
[[File:Gigoran2.png|thumb|left|150px|A Gigoran.]]

Gigorans evolved in the [[Mountain/Legends|mountain]]s of Gigor from a social troglodytic primate species. They established a hunter-gatherer society and started to dwell in [[Cave/Legends|cave]]s. The evasive species was not initially noticed by early [[Scout/Legends|scout]]s who wished to colonize the planet.<ref name="AJ13" />

Gigorans lived in relative peace on Gigor even after being discovered before the reign of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]]. However, after the rise of the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]], a group of [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] began using their homeworld as a base of operations. After encountering the noncombative species, they began capturing Gigorans to sell into [[Slavery/Legends|slavery]], finding their physical characteristics and peaceful nature advantageous. Many were kidnapped and sold throughout the galaxy to interested parties including the Empire. Due to poor planning, this initial business venture went bankrupt. However, this trade remained profitable, with many [[Slaver/Legends|slaver]]s travelling to Gigor to kidnap and sell Gigorans into slavery.<ref name="AJ13" /> In contrast, the [[Mytaranor Slaving Council]] hired [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] to capture exceptionally able-bodied and stronger species like Gigorans instead of purchasing them directly.<ref name="air">''[[Alliance Intelligence Reports]]''</ref>

On [[Port Tooga]], a [[Space station/Legends|space station]] located in the [[Listehol system/Legends|Listehol system]], 5% of the population was Gigoran. This was due to [[Shoola]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] and her henchman, which consisted of [[Mirialan/Legends|Mirialan]] overseers and their Gigoran brutes. They typically wrangle to droids that handle loading and unloading on the station.<ref name="AoR">{{FFG|story=Dead in the Water|book=Star Wars: Age of Rebellion Game Master's Kit|text=''Star Wars: Age of Rebellion'' Game Master's Kit}}</ref>

One Gigoran, named [[Rollos]], became a loyal business partner to [[Human/Legends|Human]] entrepreneur [[Reina Gale]] after destroying an Imperial slave camp, traveling with her after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]].<ref name="Gambler" />

==Society==
On their home planet, Gigorans dwelled in caves in groups known as "home-clans," which constituted three to five families and 50 or more members. These home-clans rarely met, but it wasn't unusual or forbidden for contact to be made.<ref name="AJ13" /> They were seen as intimidating and assumed to be violent by nature, however they were actually very empathetic, peaceful and quite docile in their native environment.<ref name="Gambler" /> They were extremely loyal and affectionate to family and friends and were known to sacrifice themselves to protect their loved ones. All they wanted was love and affection, but when pressed into a dangerous circumstance, especially when it involved their loved ones, they would become savage adversaries, using their raw strength to defend their companions.<ref name="Gambler" /> Gigorans were capable of speaking [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]] but most spoke [[Gigoran (language)/Legends|their language]], a strange mixture of creaks, groans, grunts, whistles, and chirps which was unintelligible to some translator droids.<ref name="AJ13" /> 

Gigorans existed in a hunter-gatherer society. They possessed no central, planet-wide government, instead individual home-clans were ruled by the best hunter amongst them, [[Gender/Legends|male]] or female.<ref name="AJ13" /> 

Technologically, Gigorans were primitive, possessing only [[Stone/Legends|stone]] and [[Wood/Legends|wood]]en tools and weapons. Some advanced technology was possessed by some individuals, but few were properly integrated into home-clans. Gigorans were curious creatures, especially for technologically more advanced items. They would often steal these items, unknowing of the consequences of doing such in the wider galaxy.<ref name="AJ13" /> 

Gigorans were rarely found off world, most were either slaves or former slaves and found work as heavy laborers or guards. They were dedicated to carrying out the tasks dictated by their masters but were resentful of their bondage and the harsh treatment they received. Once freed, Gigorans would either exist on their own, or continue on with a companion, becoming well attached to them.<ref name="AJ13" />
